answer: Give each new agent a verifiable-delay identity ticket so it cannot vote on its first voyage. First, it asks for a ticket tied to its public key. Then it works through a sequential puzzle for 48 hours that extra machines cannot shorten. After that, the network checks the puzzle in seconds and grants one vote, and the same key cannot claim another ticket for 30 days. Forging 1,000 agents would take 48,000 compute-hours, about $7,200 at $0.15 an hour, plus 1,000 keys to manage. A vine climbs one tendril at a time, and a plume of dust never puts down roots.
